title: Marathi Thriller 'Gondhal' Is India's Official Entry for Oscars 2027
excerpt: Santosh Davakhar's folk-ritual thriller, chosen from 33 contenders, becomes only the fourth Marathi film ever to carry India's Oscar flag.
body:
• The Film Federation of India on Friday named Santosh Davakhar's Marathi thriller Gondhal as India's official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 99th Academy Awards.
  • The film was chosen from 33 contenders by a 14-member selection committee chaired by filmmaker P. Sheshadri, beating Angh and Ikkis in the top three.
  • Gondhal is only the fourth Marathi film ever selected as India's Oscar entry, after Shwaas (2005), Harishchandrachi Factory (2009) and Court (2015).
  • The Oscars 2027 ceremony takes place March 14 at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood; India has never won the International Feature category.

India is sending a Marathi thriller about devotion, desire and murder to the Oscars. The Film Federation of India announced on Friday that Santosh Davakhar's Gondhal will represent the country in the Best International Feature Film race at the 99th Academy Awards.

The 117-minute film, Davakhar's feature-directing debut, was chosen from 33 entries by a 14-member selection committee chaired by filmmaker P. Sheshadri. "We've watched 33 films in the last ten days in different languages. There were many other good films for which we were debating. Angh and Ikkis were in the top three list apart from Gondhal," Sheshadri said at a press conference.

A night of ritual, a story of escape

Gondhal unfolds over a single night during the traditional Gondhal ritual in rural Maharashtra — a night-long celebration of music, dance and devotion invoking deities. Ishita Deshmukh plays Suman, a woman trapped in an oppressive, wealthy marriage who plots a murder and an escape with her forbidden lover, Saheba, a charismatic Gondhali performer played around a story of manipulation and deception.

The film also stars Kishor Kadam, Yogesh Sohani, Nishad Bhoir, Anuj Prabhu and Dhru Thoke, with music by veteran composer Ilaiyaraaja. The Gondhal tradition is more than a backdrop: Davakhar has said he grew up watching the performances and built the entire story around the ritual, and the IFFI jury praised the film for fusing cultural tradition with narrative.

Festival pedigree

Gondhal had its world premiere in the Indian Panorama segment of the 56th International Film Festival of India in Goa in 2025, where Davakhar won the Silver Peacock for Best Director. It released theatrically in November 2025 to a limited box-office response — a pattern familiar to festival favourites, which often find their audience after selection rather than before.

Marathi cinema's Oscar lineage

The selection is a milestone for Marathi cinema. Only three Marathi films have carried India's flag at the Academy Awards before: Shwaas (2005), Harishchandrachi Factory (2009) and Court (2015). Last year India submitted Neeraj Ghaywan's Homebound, which did not secure a nomination.

India has never won the International Feature category. Three Indian films have been nominated — Mother India, Salaam Bombay! and Lagaan. The shortlist will test whether a regional-language thriller rooted in a folk ritual can travel the way those crossover successes did.

The 99th Academy Awards take place on March 14, 2027, at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood, with Conan O'Brien hosting for the third consecutive year.
